preconditions.description: The number of test cases is at least 1.

preconditions.expression: all(3 <= n <= 100 for n in [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit() and int(line) >= 3])
preconditions.description: Each test case starts with an integer n (3 ≤ n ≤ 100) representing half the number of players.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.strip()) == 0 or line.strip() in ['>', '<'] for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.strip().isdigit())
preconditions.description: Each match outcome is either '>' or '<', indicating the stronger player in the match.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout.split('!')) == t + 1 for stdout in [output for output in outputs if output.strip() == '!'])
postconditions.description: The program terminates each test case with an exclamation mark (!) and flushes the output.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout.split('?')) <= 4 * n**2 + 1 for n, stdout in zip([int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit()], outputs))
postconditions.description: The program organizes at most 4n² matches per test case.

postconditions.expression: all(any('?' in line for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip()) or output.strip() == '!' for output in outputs)
postconditions.description: The program either organizes a match (with '? i j') or terminates a test case (with '!').

postconditions.expression: all(len(set(line.split()[1:]) for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip().startswith('?')) == 2 for output in outputs)
postconditions.description: Each match query includes exactly two distinct player indices.

postconditions.expression: all(any(line.strip() == '!' for line in output.splitlines()) for output in outputs)
postconditions.description: Each test case output ends with an exclamation mark (!).
Each test case output contains at least one line (either a match or termination).
